analysis.title: The cybersecurity bull lives on (AI boom's unintended winner)
key_insights: Buying dips toward the 50-day moving average and trendline support has remained a profitable strategy in CIBR. Cybersecurity is showing relative resilience while much of the AI trade has struggled.

SG estimates global information security spending at roughly $240B in 2026, growing 12.5-13.3% annually, a fifth consecutive year of double-digit growth. Security is about 13% of IT budgets, up from 8.6% in 2020.
The AI-amplified cybersecurity market is projected to grow from $49B in 2025 to $160B in 2029 (per SG).

BofA cites the latest PHP2Shell vulnerabilities as a sign that AI can discover and exploit security flaws at machine speed. This raises the need for faster detection, vulnerability management, threat hunting and AI-powered security operations.

SG estimates roughly 76% of malware now exhibits AI-driven polymorphism, and AI is increasingly automating phishing, credential theft and exploitation. Gartner expects AI cybersecurity spending to nearly double in 2026.
BofA's latest CIO survey shows cyber budgets expected to grow 7% in 2027, outpacing overall software spending. Half of CIOs expect growth above 7%.
BofA has raised price targets on CrowdStrike, Check Point, SailPoint and Zscaler, among other cybersecurity names.

A World Economic Forum report finds more than half of organizations invest in cybersecurity mainly in response to crises, and only 8% cite demonstrated returns as the trigger. The Market Ear reads this as a reactive market with room for a more sustained spending cycle as security moves from IT cost to strategic investment.
